 G.P. for Finance & Planning
 G.P. for Land Acquisition
Order:
Heard learned counsel for the petitioners and learned Assistant Government Pleader for Land Acquisition.
With the consent of both the parties, the Writ Petition is disposed of at the stage of admission.

2. The Writ Petition is filed seeking to declare the inaction on the part of the respondents in paying the amount of compensation awarded in respect of the lands, which were acquired from petitioners by passing a consent Award No.01/2021-2022 dated 15.09.2021 for an extent of Ac.0.87 cents situated at Chiramana Village, A.S.Peta Mandal, SPSR Nellore District, as illegal, arbitrary and violative of the rights guaranteed under Articles 19, 21 and 300-A of the Constitution of India and for a consequential direction to the respondents to pay the compensation amount of Rs.5,23,636/-
with the interest @ 15% p.a., from date of Award 15.09.2021 till the date of payment as per the Sec.80 of the Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013(for short 'the Act').
3.

entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: The learned counsel for the petitioners with reference to the averments made in the Writ Petition submits that the petitioners are the absolute owners and possessors of the subject lands.
He submits that the said lands were acquired for the purpose of Somasila Project.
He submits that an Award No.01/2021-2022 dated 15.09.2021 was passed granting a compensation of Rs.5,23,636/-.

He submits that the 5th respondent addressed a letter to the 6th respondent to take immediate action for preparation of necessary bill etc., for payment of compensation to the concerned awardees vide proceedings dated 28.09.2021.
But the compensation has not been paid to the petitioners.

1 further submits that non-payment of compensation is unjust, arbitrary and the delay in payment of compensation is causing serious prejudice and irreparable loss to the petitioners.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: He submits that under those circumstances, the petitioners are constrained to approach this Court seeking appropriate directions.
He also submits that this Court in similar circumstances disposed of W.P.No.1758 of 2023 vide Order dated 30.01.2023 and that an Order on the same lines may be passed.

4. Learned Assistant Government Pleader for Land Acquisition, on the other hand placed a copy of the written instructions dated 21.07.2023 received from the 6th respondent and on perusal of the same, it would appear that there is no dispute with regard to passing of Award referred to above and non-payment of compensation to the petitioners in respect of the subject matter lands.
However, it appears that due to insufficient funds, the payments have not been made to the petitioners.

The relevant portion of the instructions reads thus:
"In view of the above Award enquiry has been conducted by the then staff of this office and prepared Consent Award for lands an extent of Ac.0.87 cents for Rs.5,23,636/-( Rupees Five lakhs twenty three thousand six hundred and thirty six only) the same was approved by the Special Collector, TGP, Nellore.

After approval of award bill was prepared an amount of Rs.5,23,636/- (Rupees Five lakhs twenty three thousand six hundred and thirty six only) and submitted in CFMS Portal on 29.08.2022 vide CFMS No.2022- 1248662 and sent to Assistant Pay and Accounts Officer, Works and Project-1, Nellore and same was returned due to (DDO as per Art.39 & 50 of AP Financial Code. Vol.1.).
After the New CFMS Bill was migrated vide bill No.2023- 231379.
It is further submitted that the compensation amount not credit in the petitioners account to till date.

The bill was submitted to CFMS portal in time."
5. This Court has considered the submissions and perused the material on record.
There is no dispute with regard to taking over possession of the lands in question and passing of Award.
The petitioners are deprived of their lands and it is unfortunate that the compensation has not been paid though the Award was passed in 2021.

Though the reasons are obvious as noted from the written instructions, the same cannot be appreciated and delay in payment effects the rights of the petitioners guaranteed under Articles 14 and 21 of the Constitution of India.
6.

In the aforesaid view of the matter and as there is no dispute about the petitioners' entitlement,
this Court deems it appropriate to dispose of the Writ Petition with a direction to the respondents 1,2 and 4 to 6 to pay the compensation amount to the petitioners, pursuant to the Award dated 15.09.2021, as expeditiously as possible, at any rate, within a period of four (4) weeks from the date of receipt of a copy of this Order.
Needless to state that this Order would not preclude the petitioners from claiming interest in respect of the awarded compensation before the appropriate Forum.

The Writ Petition is disposed of accordingly, with the above directions.
There shall be no order as to costs.
As a sequel, all the pending miscellaneous applications in the above writ petition, if any, shall stand closed.
